papers.title: Translational Toxicology of N-Isopropylbutylone: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Assessment of a New Synthetic Cathinone.
papers.abstract: The novel psychoactive substance (NPS) phenomenon represents a major global problem. Despite the methodical inclusion of new analogues in lists of controlled drugs, new compounds continue to circulate, frequently resulting in fatal intoxications. The emergence of N-isopropyl butylone (NiPB) in 2024, found as an adulterant in methamphetamine-based products, underscores the rapidly evolving landscape of NPSs. Despite its structural similarity to potent monoamine transporter inhibitors, specific pharmacological data and information on its effects in consumers are currently lacking. This study aim
papers.summary: This study characterizes N-isopropylbutylone (NiPB), a new synthetic cathinone that appeared in 2024 as an adulterant in methamphetamine products, using combined in vivo and in silico approaches. The work provides pharmacological and toxicological data on a compound with structural similarity to potent monoamine transporter inhibitors but previously lacking specific effect information. It aims to fill the data gap on this emerging novel psychoactive substance to inform risk assessment.

papers.title: Predicting Rates of Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with Brain- and Cardiac-Imputed Transcripts.
papers.abstract: Severe cognitive decline due to dementia is an important clinical indicator signaling neurodegeneration. Predicting cognitive decline rates can be useful in establishing prognosis and modifying treatment regimens. The rate of decline is highly variable across patients with dementia and may be determined by an interplay of many factors. This variability poses challenges to existing tools for predicting disease progression. Changes in heart and brain tissue have been associated with cognitive decline, yet tissue-specific molecular data are difficult to obtain. In this study, we sought to estimat
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The study uses computational imputation to estimate tissue-specific gene expression in brain and heart from more accessible data, then tests whether these imputed transcripts can predict the rate of cognitive decline in older adults. It aims to address the difficulty of obtaining brain and heart tissue by leveraging imputed molecular profiles as predictors of dementia progression. The work suggests that combining brain- and cardiac-derived transcriptomic signals may improve prognosis of cognitive decline trajectories.

papers.title: Neuroprotective Potential of the Edible Seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea: Bioactivity Coupled LC-MS/MS, Metabolomics Annotation, Validation, and Network Pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a global impact, highlighting an urgent need for effective dietary therapeutic agents for the development of brain-healthy functional foods and medicines. This study focuses on the edible red alga Pterocladiella capillacea from Zhanjiang, China, investigating its anti-neuronal injury activity, active principles, and underlying mechanisms. Methods: Based on antioxidant and neuroprotection evaluations and column fractioning, bioactivity-coupled liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (Bio-LC-MS/MS) was emplo
papers.summary: This study investigates the edible red seaweed Pterocladiella capillacea for neuroprotective compounds relevant to Alzheimer's disease. Using bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with LC-MS/MS and metabolomics annotation, the authors identify active principles and use network pharmacology to predict their mechanisms of action against neuronal injury.

papers.title: Measuring AI Progress in Drug Discovery: A Reproducible Leaderboard for the Tox21 Challenge.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has fundamentally transformed fields such as computer vision and natural language processing since the early 2010s and has strongly influenced biomedical research. For drug discovery specifically, a key inflection point─akin to vision's "ImageNet moment"─arrived in 2015, when deep neural networks surpassed traditional approaches in the Tox21 Data Challenge. This milestone accelerated the adoption of deep learning methods across the pharmaceutical industry, and today, most major companies have integrated these approaches into their research pipelines. Following the conclusion of t
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper introduces a reproducible leaderboard for the Tox21 Challenge, the 2015 benchmark where deep neural networks first outperformed traditional methods in predicting chemical toxicity, marking a key milestone for AI in drug discovery. The leaderboard aims to standardize evaluation and track progress of AI methods on this foundational task over time. It provides a shared benchmark to compare new models against historical results in a transparent, reproducible way.

papers.title: Efficient Discovery of Potent AKR1B10 Inhibitors Using Co-folding Model Boltz-2.
papers.abstract: Although affinity prediction of protein-ligand binding remains an important challenge, cofolding models are expected to make virtual screening more effective for drug discovery and development. To verify the effectiveness of selecting a tractable number of candidates from a compound library using cofolding models, we strove to identify a novel inhibitory active compound using Boltz-2, a representative cofolding model, for aldo-keto reductase 1B10 (AKR1B10), which is highly expressed in various cancers. Consequently, of the 40 candidate compounds obtained after narrowing-down 867 candidates fro
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study tested whether the co-folding model Boltz-2 can effectively prioritize compounds for virtual screening against the cancer-associated enzyme AKR1B10. Starting from 867 candidates, the authors narrowed to 40 compounds and experimentally identified novel potent AKR1B10 inhibitors, demonstrating that co-folding-based affinity prediction can streamline hit discovery.

papers.title: Persistent Local Laplacian Prediction of Protein-Ligand Binding Affinities.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of protein-ligand binding affinity remains a central challenge in structure-based drug discovery. The effectiveness of machine learning models critically depends on the quality of molecular representations, for which advanced mathematical frameworks provide powerful tools. In this work, we employ a novel mathematical theory, termed the persistent local Laplacian (PLL), to construct molecular descriptors that capture localized geometric and topological features of biomolecular structures. The PLL framework addresses key limitations of traditional topological data analysis me
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce a new mathematical framework called persistent local Laplacian (PLL) to build molecular descriptors that capture local geometric and topological features of protein-ligand complexes. These descriptors are used to train machine learning models for predicting binding affinity, addressing limitations of traditional topological data analysis. The work aims to improve structure-based drug discovery by providing richer molecular representations.

papers.title: The Glyco-Code Molecular Template Instructively Guides Skeletal and Neural Development, Tissue Regeneration and Dynamic Repair Responses Following Trauma and Disease.
papers.abstract: Glycosaminoglycans encode instructional information that cells can decipher to regulate tissue development, repair responses, regeneration and recovery of tissue function following trauma or disease. This information has been termed the glyco-code and is a road map for tissue development and repair. This review shows that a clearer understanding of the glyco-code will support improved strategies in repair biology, particularly in skeletal and neural repair, regeneration, and therapeutic biomaterial design. Emerging therapeutic approaches for peripheral nerve repair increasingly combine multimo
papers.summary: This review argues that glycosaminoglycans carry instructional information—termed the glyco-code—that cells decode to direct tissue development, repair, and regeneration. It surveys how understanding this code could improve strategies for skeletal and neural repair, including the design of therapeutic biomaterials and emerging combination approaches for peripheral nerve repair.

papers.title: Innovative design and development of novel thiazole-paracetamol hybrids as COX inhibitors and immunomodulatory activity: design, synthesis, SAR, in vitro biological evaluation, and molecular docking analysis.
papers.abstract: The hybridization approach was employed to design a single pharmacophore based on the conjugation of paracetamol with thiazole derivatives, yielding thiazole-paracetamol hybrid derivatives 4-11 that utilize a linker from hydrazone (-C[double bond, length as m-dash]N-NH) and azo (-N[double bond, length as m-dash]N-) linkers, serving as the hydrogen bond donor/acceptor binding site. The structure of the designed derivatives was fully characterized and confirmed using analytical data (IR, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR), and elemental analysis. The anti-inflammatory potential of the synthesized hybrids was
papers.summary: This paper describes the design and synthesis of hybrid molecules that combine paracetamol with thiazole derivatives via hydrazone or azo linkers, aiming to create dual-acting COX inhibitors with immunomodulatory activity. The compounds were chemically characterized and evaluated in vitro for anti-inflammatory potential, with structure-activity relationships and molecular docking analysis supporting the binding to COX targets. The work is a medicinal chemistry proof-of-concept for paracetamol-thiazole hybrids as anti-inflammatory agents.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used LC-HRMS/MS molecular networking (GNPS) to profile metabolites from Scoparia dulcis, an edible medicinal herb, then combined network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations with experimental validation to identify bioactive constituents and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The integrated approach links specific phytochemicals to inflammatory targets and pathways, providing a mechanistic basis for the herb's traditional use.

papers.title: LASSBio-classFLOW: A Semiautomated KNIME Workflow for Classification Model Benchmarking and Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Machine learning-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (ML-QSAR) modeling requires consistent data preparation, validation, and model comparison. We present LASSBio-classFLOW, an open, modular, and semiautomated KNIME workflow for classification-based ligand screening. It integrates basic molecular structure preparation, configurable class assignment, descriptors and fingerprints calculation, dataset partitioning, hyperparameter optimization of nine algorithms, interactive performance evaluation, user-guided model selection, and external-library prediction. As an example, the work
papers.summary: LASSBio-classFLOW is an open, modular KNIME workflow that semi-automates the entire ML-QSAR classification pipeline, from molecular preparation and descriptor calculation through hyperparameter tuning of nine algorithms, model evaluation, and virtual screening of external libraries. It aims to standardize and simplify model benchmarking for ligand-based screening, making rigorous QSAR workflows more accessible to non-programmers.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related cl
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning has been applied across amyloid research, from predicting which protein sequences are likely to form amyloid fibrils to supporting structural studies and the design of inhibitor drugs. It frames ML as a transformative paradigm for tackling amyloid-related neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, organizing the field into sequence prediction, structural biology, and inhibitor design domains.

papers.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitory evaluation of prenylated flavonoids from peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) shells: in vitro and in silico molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Sustainable agriculture has become a crucial priority because the improper management of agricultural waste currently contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, as well as soil and air pollution. The shells of Arachis hypogaea L., which is commonly discarded as an agricultural by-product, have been reported to contain various secondary metabolites, including flavonoids, stilbenes, triterpenoids, etc. This work led to the isolation of two new prenylated flavonoids, arachisflavones A (1) and B (2), together with five prenylated flavones (3-7), two prenylated chalcones (8-9), and three prenylated f
papers.summary: This study isolated two new prenylated flavonoids (arachisflavones A and B) along with several known prenylated flavones and chalcones from peanut shells, an agricultural waste product. The compounds were tested for xanthine oxidase inhibition in vitro and evaluated by molecular docking, identifying prenylated flavonoids as potential xanthine oxidase inhibitors. The work highlights peanut shells as a sustainable source of bioactive compounds with possible relevance to gout or hyperuricemia management.

papers.title: Rational design and synthesis of furan-based Schiff base quinazolin-4-amine hybrids: spectral elucidation, molecular docking, DFT studies, and in silico ADMET-antioxidant study.
papers.abstract: In this work, a new series of furan-based quinazoline-4-amine hydrazone (Schiff base) derivatives (4a-h) was rationally designed and synthesized in good yields (84-90%) through a multistep route involving nucleophilic aromatic substitution, Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling, and hydrazone/Schiff base condensation reactions. The synthesized compounds were characterized by FT-IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and ESI-mass spectrometry, which confirmed the proposed structures. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed to optimize the molecular geometries and to derive frontier molecular orbital
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of eight furan-based quinazoline-4-amine Schiff base hybrids using a multistep route and characterized them spectroscopically. They then used DFT calculations, molecular docking, and in silico ADMET/antioxidant predictions to assess the compounds' potential as drug-like antioxidants. The work is purely computational and synthetic, with no experimental biological validation reported.

papers.title: NU-1025 modulates immunogenic cell death in bladder cancer: A multi-omics insight.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has shown limited efficacy in bladder cancer, underscoring the need for therapeutic strategies that enhance tumor immunogenicity. Immunogenic cell death (ICD) can stimulate adaptive immunity and remodel the tumor microenvironment, yet its comprehensive landscape and druggable potential in bladder cancer remain unexplored. Here, we performed integrative bioinformatics analysis of transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO bladder cancer cohorts to characterize ICD-associated subtypes, construct a prognostic risk model, and analyze immune infiltration. Connectivity Map (CMa
papers.summary: This study used integrative bioinformatics on TCGA and GEO bladder cancer transcriptomes to characterize immunogenic cell death (ICD)-associated subtypes, build a prognostic risk model, and profile immune infiltration. The authors then used Connectivity Map analysis to identify NU-1025 as a compound that may modulate ICD in bladder cancer. The work is exploratory and computational, proposing a candidate drug and risk model without experimental validation.

papers.title: qcGEM: A Graph-Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness.
papers.abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI-based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum-chemistry-aware graph-based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning. Through a specially designed model ar
papers.summary: qcGEM introduces a graph-based molecular representation that incorporates quantum chemistry-derived physical priors into the embedding, aiming to overcome the lack of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations. This quantum-chemistry-aware embedding is designed to improve predictive performance in AI-driven drug discovery while also making learned representations more mechanistically interpretable. The work addresses a key limitation of existing molecular representations for practical and human-usable AI models.

papers.title: AI-integrated iPSC multi-omics: advancing phenotype discovery and drug target identification in rare diseases.
papers.abstract: Rare diseases represent a major unmet medical need, yet the development of therapeutics for these diseases is limited by small patient cohorts, fragmented data, and uncertain disease mechanisms. Recent advances that combine patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models with multi-omics profiling and artificial intelligence offer a robust approach for phenotype definition and drug target identification that requires only minimal patient material. By integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, machine learning can produce disease-relevant molecular signatures, iden
papers.summary: This review discusses how combining patient-derived iPSC models with multi-omics profiling (transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics) and AI/machine learning can overcome the challenges of rare disease research, such as small patient cohorts and limited material. The integrated approach enables disease-relevant molecular signature discovery and drug target identification, advancing phenotype definition for rare diseases.

papers.title: Advancing Pregnancy and Pediatric Science through the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network.
papers.abstract: Human gestation is characterized by dynamic changes in maternal physiology and maturation of tissue functions before and after birth. The fetus and neonate are highly dependent upon transfer of maternal nutrients via the placenta and lactating mammary gland, which frequently involve selective membrane transporter proteins. At the same time, developmental changes in fetal and infant transport mechanisms critical for regulating absorption at the intestinal and blood-brain barriers are occurring. Coordinate regulation of cellular entry and efflux of nutrients, supplements, and xenobiotics, includ
papers.summary: This paper describes the NIH Transporter Elucidation Network, a new initiative aimed at understanding how membrane transporter proteins change during pregnancy and early development. It highlights how dynamic maternal physiology and the maturation of fetal and infant transport systems in the placenta, mammary gland, intestine, and blood-brain barrier govern nutrient transfer and drug disposition. The network's goal is to advance research on these developmental transport mechanisms to improve maternal, fetal, and pediatric health.

papers.title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences.
papers.abstract: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 mi
papers.summary: CLEAN DB is a new database that provides predicted enzyme function annotations for over 55 million protein sequences, addressing the gap between the vast number of known sequences and the small fraction with experimentally characterized functions. It leverages AI-based prediction methods to assign enzyme functions at high throughput, offering broad coverage of sequence space. This resource aims to support enzyme discovery and rational design by making functional annotations widely accessible.

papers.title: From artificial intelligence promise to translational practice in drug discovery: Reproducibility, validation and evidence-based implementation.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support drug discovery, but benchmark performance alone does not establish experimental, operational or clinical benefit. This keynote review distinguishes predictive generalization, experimental confirmation, workflow utility and clinical outcomes, separating demonstrated failures from missing validation. We critically examine quantitative case studies of benchmark bias, prospective hit finding and clinical development, alongside data quality, reproducibility, uncertainty and governance. Practical recommendations link each intended use to appropriate comparato
papers.summary: This keynote review argues that strong AI benchmark performance in drug discovery does not guarantee experimental, operational, or clinical benefit, and it separates genuine failures from cases where validation is simply missing. It critically examines case studies on benchmark bias, prospective hit finding, and clinical development, along with issues of data quality, reproducibility, uncertainty, and governance. The authors offer practical recommendations that tie each intended use of an AI model to appropriate comparators and validation standards.

papers.title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across neuro-oncology to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data, addressing tumor heterogeneity that conventional approaches struggle to capture. It argues that AI can deliver quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights, and it represents a joint effort across response assessment frameworks.

papers.title: Integrated Experimental and Computational Investigation of Fluorinated Benzoylthiourea Derivatives: Structural Characterization, Hirshfeld Surface Analysis, Antioxidant Activity, and MAO-B Inhibitory Potential for Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives, namely FBTU1-FBTU3, were successfully synthesized in 79-86% yields and fully characterized using spectroscopic techniques including FT-IR, 1H, 13C and 19F NMR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, elemental analysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD). All three compounds crystallize in the monoclinic system (P21/c for FBTU1 and FBTU3; P21/n for FBTU2) with Z = 4. The crystallographic analysis revealed well-defined molecular geometries stabilized by intramolecular and intermolecular interactions. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses ind
papers.summary: The authors synthesized and structurally characterized three novel fluorinated benzoylthiourea derivatives (FBTU1–FBTU3) using spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction, then analyzed their crystal packing via Hirshfeld surface and energy framework methods. They further evaluated these compounds for antioxidant activity and MAO-B inhibitory potential as a possible route toward Parkinson's disease therapeutics. The work is a combined experimental and computational characterization study of a small compound series.

papers.title: Comparative anthelmintic activity of artemisinin, dihydroartemisinin, and artesunate against sheep gastrointestinal nematodes: in vitro evaluation and exploratory β-tubulin molecular modeling.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal nematode infections are an important constraint on small-ruminant production, and increasing anthelmintic resistance has intensified the search for alternative therapeutic compounds. Artemisinin and its derivatives have demonstrated activity against several helminth species, although comparative information regarding their effects on gastrointestinal nematodes remains limited. This study compared the in vitro anthelmintic activity of artemisinin (ART), dihydroartemisinin (DHA), and artesunate (ARTE) and explored β-tubulin as a candidate molecular target using complementary com
papers.summary: This study compared the in vitro anthelmintic activity of artemisinin, dihydroartemisinin, and artesunate against sheep gastrointestinal nematodes, finding differences in potency among the three compounds. The authors also used molecular modeling to explore β-tubulin as a possible drug target, suggesting a mechanistic hypothesis for the observed activity. The work supports further investigation of artemisinin derivatives as alternatives amid rising anthelmintic resistance.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of Alzheimer's disease molecular networks with circadian regulators for prioritization of drug repurposing candidates.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by complex molecular mechanisms. Growing evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption contributes to disease progression and interacts with pathogenic pathways. Although multi-omics resources, compound perturbation profiles, and pharmacological bioactivity data are increasingly available, their integrative use for drug repurposing prioritization in AD, particularly with explicit consideration of circadian rhythm, remains limited.ObjectiveThis study aimed to prioritize drug repurposing candida
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics Alzheimer's disease network data with circadian rhythm regulators and compound perturbation/pharmacological bioactivity profiles to prioritize drug repurposing candidates. By explicitly incorporating circadian biology into network-based analysis, the authors identify compounds that may act on AD-relevant pathways linked to circadian disruption. The work demonstrates a framework for combining diverse data resources to nominate repurposing candidates for further validation.

papers.title: Predicting Synergistic and Antagonistic Micellization Effects in Surfactant Blends for Optimized Formulation Design.
papers.abstract: Surfactant mixtures exhibit non-ideal interactions that govern their macroscopic behavior, yet their prediction is limited by the need for experimentally derived interaction parameters. Within Rubingh's Regular Solution Approximation (RST), these interactions are described by the parameter β, which is typically obtained by fitting experimental mixture data, restricting its applicability in large-scale formulation design. In this work, a computational hybrid approach combining machine learning with thermodynamic modeling is introduced to enable end-to-end prediction and optimization of surfacta
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present a hybrid machine-learning plus thermodynamic-modeling approach that predicts the interaction parameter β in surfactant blends without requiring experimental mixture data, enabling end-to-end prediction of synergistic versus antagonistic micellization. This allows rapid in silico screening and optimization of surfactant formulations, replacing the traditional bottleneck of fitting β from experiments.

papers.title: Assessing the Generalizability of Machine Learning and Physics-Based Methods with DNA-Encoded Libraries.
papers.abstract: Predicting protein-ligand binding is a central challenge in computational drug discovery, and while machine learning (ML) and cofolding methods have advanced rapidly, their ability to generalize beyond training or parametrization regimes remains insufficiently understood. DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) enable ultralarge screening of billions of molecules simultaneously, providing a useful testbed for evaluating these approaches at scale. A recent NeurIPS competition revealed that even top-performing ML models trained on DEL data failed at generalizing to out-of-distribution (OOD) chemical space.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper evaluates how well machine learning and physics-based protein-ligand binding prediction methods generalize beyond their training or parametrization regimes, using DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) as a large-scale testbed. It builds on a NeurIPS competition finding that top ML models trained on DEL data failed to generalize to out-of-distribution chemical space, highlighting a key limitation for computational drug discovery.

papers.title: CUE: A Chemical Uncertainty-Aware Embedding Framework for Multimodal Drug Selectivity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug selectivity is critical for prioritizing candidate compounds with reduced off-target effects in AI-based drug discovery. Although selectivity can be inferred indirectly from drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction, cumulative errors from affinity predictions across multiple targets can reduce reliability, motivating the development of methods that directly predict compound-level selectivity. We propose a Chemical Uncertainty-aware Embedding (CUE) framework that integrates molecular fingerprints and 2D molecular structure image embeddings. The two modalities are combin
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The paper introduces CUE, a multimodal framework that combines molecular fingerprints with 2D molecular structure image embeddings to directly predict drug selectivity, rather than inferring it indirectly from drug-target affinity predictions. The approach incorporates chemical uncertainty awareness to improve reliability, aiming to help prioritize compounds with fewer off-target effects in AI-driven drug discovery.

papers.title: AI Accelerated Chemical Screening Integrates ChemBERTa to Identify Repositionable CASP4 Inhibitors via MD Simulations and MM/PBSA Analysis.
papers.abstract: This study employed an integrated ligand-based virtual screening pipeline to identify potential CASP4 inhibitors from the DrugBank database, leveraging docking-score prioritization, SMILES-derived ChemBERTa embeddings, and key physicochemical descriptors. Building on this foundation, the workflow incorporated virtual screening, cheminformatics modeling, PK-PD evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA free-energy analysis to systematically prioritize repurposed DrugBank compounds for CASP4-targeted Alzheimer's disease therapy. A Random Forest classifier trained
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This study combines ligand-based virtual screening with ChemBERTa SMILES embeddings and a Random Forest classifier to prioritize DrugBank compounds as potential CASP4 inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease. Hits were further validated through docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA free-energy analysis, yielding repositionable candidate compounds.

papers.title: Language of Toxicity: An eXplainable Artificial Intelligence Approach.
papers.abstract: Toxicity prediction in small molecules represents a fundamental challenge in drug development and chemical safety assessment. Traditional approaches heavily rely on predefined molecular descriptors or fingerprints, potentially limiting the ability to capture complex and nonlinear structure-activity relationships. Here, we present a descriptor-free, language-inspired framework that can be applied to different toxicity prediction tasks within a unified architecture. The model proposed combines a multiscale Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layer to capture chemical patterns at different scales
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors present a descriptor-free, language-inspired deep learning framework for predicting small-molecule toxicity. It uses a multiscale CNN to capture chemical patterns at different scales within a unified architecture applicable to multiple toxicity tasks, aiming to overcome limitations of predefined molecular descriptors and fingerprints.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer integrative analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, to characterize its expression and role across tumor types. It then uses structure-based drug design to screen buckwheat-derived natural compounds as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work combines multi-omics cancer data with computational docking to nominate natural-product candidates targeting AKT1.

papers.title: Beyond global drug-likeness: The FamDLike framework as a target family-specific drug-likeness score.
papers.abstract: Drug-likeness is a central metric which is used to evaluate the physicochemical profile of small molecules either as a filter for virtual screening or, more recently, as a reward function in generative design tasks. Established scores such as QED are widely adopted for these purposes, although the ligands of different therapeutic target families occupy different regions of physicochemical space. Applying a single global drug-likeness criterion can therefore systematically reward some target classes while penalising others, narrowing the chemical space considered druglike in a way that may not
papers.summary: The authors introduce FamDLike, a drug-likeness scoring framework that is tailored to specific therapeutic target families rather than using a single global criterion like QED. Because ligands for different target families occupy distinct physicochemical regions, global scores can systematically favor some target classes over others; FamDLike aims to correct this bias in virtual screening and generative design.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the structure of the antifungal protein NFAP2, which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins like glutamate decarboxylase and mitochondrial ATP synthase, to guide a structure-based drug repurposing screen against Candida albicans. The approach leverages existing compounds with known safety profiles to identify potential new antifungals, addressing the urgent need for therapies against invasive fungal infections amid rising resistance.

papers.title: Fragment OptimizationSimple SMILES String Manipulation Strategies to Optimize a Hit or Fragment.
papers.abstract: AI/ML-based tools for generative and predictive modeling have become important contributors to small molecule drug discovery, enabling virtual compound design and ADME profiling prior to synthesis. Alongside these methods, simpler nonlearned strategies based on direct SMILES manipulation remain useful, particularly for low data targets. Herein is described a method for fragment optimization in which characters of a SMILES string are systematically replaced with alternative SMILES patterns to generate atom-type swaps, ring expansion/contraction, cyclization, ring opening, and fragment grafts. T
papers.summary: The paper describes a simple, non-AI method for fragment optimization in drug discovery that works by systematically replacing characters in a SMILES string with alternative SMILES patterns. This generates diverse structural modifications such as atom-type swaps, ring expansion/contraction, cyclization, ring opening, and fragment grafts. The approach is positioned as a useful alternative for low-data targets where AI/ML generative models may struggle.

papers.title: Design and Synthesis of New Thiazole Derivatives for Alzheimer's Disease Therapy as a Potential Cholinesterase Inhibitor; Toxicity Prediction and Molecular Docking Studies and Biological Evaluation.
papers.abstract: In this study, thiazole derivatives 13-23 were synthesized as novel cholinesterase inhibitors. Their structures were elucidated using 1H-NMR, 13C-NMR, and elemental analysis techniques. The binding positions and efficiencies of the designed compounds on the enzyme were investigated through molecular docking studies, and the properties of ADMET were examined using computational methods. Cytotoxicity analyses of the synthesized compounds were performed to screen their inhibitory effects on acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) in vitro. It has been determined that these co
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis and evaluation of a series of novel thiazole derivatives (13-23) as potential cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease therapy. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, assessed for AChE and BChE inhibition in vitro, and analyzed via molecular docking and ADMET predictions to explore binding modes and drug-likeness. The work identifies thiazole scaffolds with cholinesterase inhibitory activity, though the abstract is truncated and specific potency data are not fully detailed.

papers.title: Sartans and Bisartans: Expanding Therapeutic Horizons Through Broad Receptor Interactions and Repurposing Potential.
papers.abstract: Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), also known as sartans, are a family of highly selective angiotensin II type 1 receptor antagonists commonly prescribed to individuals with hypertension, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. Additionally, the discovery and facile synthesis of bisartans, a novel class of ARB antihypertensives, have shown therapeutic promise for cardiovascular diseases. Recent computational and network pharmacology studies have shown a broader receptor interactome, encompassing alpha-adrenergic receptors, and delta- and mu-opioid receptors, highlighting the polypharmaco
papers.summary: This review examines angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans) and the newer bisartan class, highlighting recent computational and network pharmacology evidence that these drugs interact with a broader set of receptors than previously recognized, including alpha-adrenergic and opioid receptors. This polypharmacology suggests potential for repurposing sartans beyond cardiovascular disease, though the findings are largely computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) using combined computational and experimental approaches. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggest PBSA-7 binds NorA and MepA efflux pumps, and in vitro assays support its ability to inhibit efflux activity. The work highlights a natural-product-derived scaffold for combating antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in hepatitis: Advances in diagnosis, treatment optimization, and prognostic prediction.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis remains a major global health challenge and an important contributor to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality worldwide. Early diagnosis, effective treatment selection, and accurate prognostic stratification remain critical unmet needs in clinical hepatology. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising approach to addressing these challenges through the integration and analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous biomedical datasets. This narrative review synthesizes advances in artificial i
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how machine learning and deep learning are being applied to hepatitis care, covering early diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognostic prediction. It highlights that AI can integrate large, heterogeneous biomedical datasets to address unmet clinical needs in hepatology, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific findings or validation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: From Molecular Profiling to Personalized Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease imposing a substantial health and economic burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to address CRS complexity in both clinical and research settings. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase for peer-reviewed articles utilizing machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing, with a focus on molecular-level or immunologic mechanisms in CRS. Thirty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis. Our results de
papers.summary: This systematic review examines 31 studies applying machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing to chronic rhinosinusitis, focusing on molecular and immunologic mechanisms. It maps how AI is being used to dissect disease heterogeneity and move toward personalized clinical management, though the evidence base remains limited in size.

papers.title: Identification of YES1 Inhibitors From Approved Drugs Using a Multimodal Deep Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: While anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) drugs, including trastuzumab improve the prognosis of patients with HER2-positive cancers, acquired resistance by cancer cells remains a significant clinical challenge. We had previously reported that YES1 is overexpressed in trastuzumab-resistant breast and lung cancer cells, and that its inhibition restores trastuzumab sensitivity. However, no approved drug specifically targets YES1. In this study, as a drug repositioning approach aimed at rapid clinical application, we constructed a machine learning model capable of learning the int
papers.summary: The authors built a multimodal deep learning framework to identify existing approved drugs that inhibit YES1, a kinase implicated in resistance to HER2-targeted therapies like trastuzumab. By screening approved drugs computationally, they aim to enable rapid drug repurposing to restore trastuzumab sensitivity in resistant breast and lung cancers. The work demonstrates a machine-learning-driven repositioning strategy for a target with no approved specific inhibitor.

papers.title: In Silico Evaluation via Virtual Screening, ADMET Profiling and Molecular Dynamics Simulations: Synthesis and Biological Activity Analysis of a Novel Antitumor PI3K Inhibitor.
papers.abstract: The PI3K plays a crucial role in cancer progression, and the development of PI3K inhibitors has always been a hot research direction in oncology. Through virtual screening and docking, potential lead compounds were identified. ADMET prediction revealed that KTC101 possesses superior pharmacokinetic profile. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that compound KTC101 could stably bind to PI3Kδ, with a binding free energy of -374.627 kJ/mol. Analysis of the metabolism of KTC101 revealed that this compound could undergo diverse phase I metabolic reactions catalyzed by hepatic CYP450 enzymes to
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a novel PI3K inhibitor (KTC101) and evaluated it computationally using virtual screening, docking, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations. KTC101 showed favorable pharmacokinetic properties and stable binding to PI3Kδ with a binding free energy of -374.627 kJ/mol. The study also characterized its phase I metabolism by hepatic CYP450 enzymes.

papers.title: Targeting a Leukemia-Relevant Protein-Protein Interface: N-Aryl Anthranilic Acids as Disruptors of the c-Myb-CBP/p300 KIX Interaction.
papers.abstract: The interaction between c-Myb and the CBP/p300 KIX domain is a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represents an attractive target for small-molecule intervention. In this study, we applied an integrated computational-experimental strategy to identify new N-aryl anthranilic acid disruptors of the c-Myb-KIX protein-protein interaction. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX (PDB 2AGH), and the top hits were further evaluated by MD simulations, MM/PBSA, FEL, and ADMET analyses. This
papers.summary: The authors used an integrated computational and experimental approach to identify N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives that disrupt the c-Myb–CBP/p300 KIX protein–protein interaction, a transcriptional event implicated in acute myeloid leukemia. A scaffold-focused library of 3,656 compounds was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX, and top hits were prioritized using MD simulations, MM/PBSA, free energy landscape analysis, and ADMET profiling. The work nominates new small-molecule scaffolds for targeting a leukemia-relevant protein–protein interface.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study characterizes the essential oil of Cotula cinerea by GC-MS (dominated by trans-thujone) and tests its anti-inflammatory effects in rats with benzylthiouracil-induced hypothyroidism. Oil treatment reduced liver and kidney indices and improved red blood cell count and hemoglobin, supported by histological and computational (molecular docking) analyses. The work is a standard ethnopharmacological evaluation of a plant extract with modest mechanistic depth.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: The authors synthesized seventeen thymol-based ester derivatives using cinnamoyl coupling chemistry and screened them for anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines and normal fibroblasts. One derivative, TM7, emerged as the most promising antiproliferative agent, and molecular docking was used to rationalize its binding to a likely target. The work is a standard medicinal chemistry design-synthesis-screen study with preliminary biological evaluation.

papers.title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi.
papers.abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction-Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus stu
papers.summary: This paper presents PTI-TAPE, a consensus framework developed through a three-round eDelphi study to standardize how computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction models are evaluated. It addresses the current lack of agreed metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction standards that make cross-study comparisons difficult. The framework aims to enable more reliable benchmarking and accelerate clinical translation of therapeutic peptides.

papers.title: Computational identification of candidate biomarkers and compounds associated with skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity improvement mediated by physical activity: an integrative multi-omics and computational chemistry study.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) underlies many chronic diseases. While physical activity improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity (IS), the underlying molecular mechanisms and targeted drug strategies remain elusive. This hypothesis-generating study integrates bioinformatics and computational chemistry using public datasets; all findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates public multi-omics datasets with computational chemistry to identify candidate biomarkers and drug-like compounds linked to physical activity-induced improvements in skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity. It is a hypothesis-generating analysis whose predictions require experimental validation.

papers.title: Redefining drug discovery: AI-driven strategies for efficient cancer therapeutics.
papers.abstract: The practice of artificial intelligence has recently expanded several social spheres, with the pharmaceutical domain leading the way. Given that AI can facilitate rational drug design, it is plausible to envision its involvement in developing pharmaceutical products from the laboratory to the patient's bedside. AI recognizes hit and lead compounds, followed by validation of therapeutic targets and optimization of molecular design. Artificial intelligence significantly impacts drug discovery and development processes, including target identification, molecule design, drug-drug interactions, dru
papers.summary: This review surveys how artificial intelligence is being applied across the cancer drug discovery pipeline, from identifying and validating therapeutic targets to designing and optimizing lead molecules. It argues that AI can accelerate rational drug design and help move candidate compounds from the lab toward clinical use. The paper is a broad overview rather than a report of new experimental results.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and genome mining strategies for activating cryptic polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces: an overview.
papers.abstract: Beneficial microbes from soil or marine habitats are promising sources for discovery of new bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture, largely through biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) that encode the production of complex natural products for drug and antibiotic discovery. However, most BGCs are transcriptionally silent under standard testing conditions and may require a complex, integrated approach for activation. In this review, we revisit previous approaches to activating BGCs, focusing on polyketides. We additionally discuss how integrating genome mining strategies with multi-omics
papers.summary: This review surveys strategies for activating silent polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces, which are a major source of natural-product drugs but often remain transcriptionally inactive under standard lab conditions. It emphasizes combining genome mining with multi-omics approaches to identify and trigger these cryptic clusters, aiming to unlock new bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) as alternatives to conventional antibiotics in the face of rising antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can help overcome key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder clinical translation.

papers.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A co
papers.summary: MolecureAI is an autonomous AI agent platform for closed-loop drug discovery that uses cost-ordered cascade evaluation to enforce chemical correctness via structural invariants rather than relying on model capability. It addresses four gaps: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. The platform aims to accelerate identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas.

papers.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
papers.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, de
papers.summary: This review surveys how network pharmacology is being used to understand how natural products from various ethnomedical traditions inhibit kidney stone formation through multiple molecular targets. It highlights that while surgery removes stones, it doesn't address the underlying metabolic, inflammatory, and crystal-injury processes that drive recurrence, and argues that multi-target natural compounds may fill this gap. The abstract is truncated, so the specific findings and conclusions of the review are not fully available.

papers.title: Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface.
papers.abstract: Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses. This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP).
papers.summary: This study presents a workflow that combines knowledge graph analysis and machine learning to prioritize putative small-molecule blockers of the interaction between the host protein PSMD11/Rpn6 and the Ebola virus glycoprotein. The approach provides a traceable path from host-factor identification to virtual screening and molecular hypothesis generation for host-directed antivirals.

papers.title: Commentary: Identification of diagnostic genes for myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury associated with metabolic syndrome through the integration of bioinformatics analysis, molecular docking and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a study that used bioinformatics integration, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify diagnostic genes linking myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury with metabolic syndrome. It highlights the study's approach to uncovering shared molecular mechanisms and potential biomarkers, while noting limitations and future directions for validating these findings.

papers.title: Investigating potential molecular mechanisms linking 6PPD-quinone exposure to Intervertebral Disc Degeneration: A network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation study.
papers.abstract: As an emerging pollutant derived from tire rubber, 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) has raised public health concerns due to widespread environmental exposure; however, its potential toxicological effects on avascular tissues such as intervertebral discs remain unclear. This study integrated network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to investigate the potential mechanisms linking 6PPD-Q exposure to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD). ADMET toxicological predictions indicated high model-predicted probabilities for SR-MMP and SR-ARE activation. Through multidimensio
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict how the environmental pollutant 6PPD-quinone might contribute to intervertebral disc degeneration. The authors identify candidate molecular targets and pathways, suggesting mitochondrial membrane potential and antioxidant response activation as potential mechanisms. The work is entirely computational and provides hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Potential Molecular Links Between Benzophenone-3 and Breast Cancer: Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Molecular Modeling, and Gene Expression Validation.
papers.abstract: Benzophenone-3 (BP-3) is a widely used ultraviolet filter with potential carcinogenic concern, but its molecular link with breast cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate targets and potential molecular links between BP-3 and breast cancer using toxicological prediction, machine learning, molecular modeling, and gene expression analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, machine learning, molecular docking, and gene expression analysis to identify candidate molecular targets linking the UV filter benzophenone-3 (BP-3) to breast cancer. The authors propose potential target genes and pathways through which BP-3 exposure might contribute to breast carcinogenesis, offering hypotheses for future experimental work. The findings are computational and correlative, requiring wet-lab validation.

papers.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
papers.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) as a molecular link between ectopic lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, a key driver of lumbar spinal stenosis. The authors propose that statins, by targeting this pathway, could be repurposed to treat the condition. The work combines mechanistic investigation with a drug-repurposing angle.

papers.title: Editorial: Exploring untapped potential: innovations in drug repurposing.
papers.summary: This editorial introduces a special issue on drug repurposing, highlighting innovations that expand the use of existing drugs for new therapeutic indications. It likely surveys emerging computational and experimental strategies, including data integration and AI-driven approaches, that accelerate repurposing discovery. As an editorial, it provides a high-level overview rather than new primary data.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study combines a 3D convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder with LSTM-based molecular generation to design novel rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique candidates were generated and screened via pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates a deep-learning pipeline for de novo drug design but reports only computational candidates without experimental validation.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study computationally screened 29 flavonoids and one FDA-approved drug for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, then used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to identify strong inhibitors of PCSK9, a key receptor in lipid regulation. The work highlights promising natural flavonoid candidates for lowering lipids, though experimental validation is still needed.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-scale computational docking and in silico analyses to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of lung cancer-associated protein targets in NSCLC. The work identifies candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding and drug-like properties, proposing them as starting points for further experimental validation. It is a purely computational screening study without wet-lab confirmation.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides
papers.abstract: The identification of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13) inducing peptides is crucial for accelerating drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening methods remain time-consuming and costly. To address these limitations, various machine learning and deep learning models have been developed, yet their performance is still constrained by the limited availability of experimentally validated data. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation (GDA) framework and predictor, GDA-Pred, to improve the predi
papers.summary: The authors present GDA-Pred, a framework that uses generative AI to create synthetic peptide data, augmenting the limited experimentally validated datasets for IL-6 and IL-13-inducing peptides. This augmentation is then used to train improved machine learning/deep learning predictors for identifying immunomodulatory peptides relevant to drug discovery. The key finding is that generative data augmentation boosts predictive performance over models trained on the small original datasets.
